Short Questions:
- True/False (Letters).
- Memo types (Informational, Analyst).
- Short definition.
Long Questions:
- How to write an abstract of thesis.
- Five points of Application letter.
- True/False.
- How to impress your reader (Resume).

Thesis unit question (3 marks). Letter blanks (3 marks) - identifying reader/customer/writer roles. Negotiation blanks (3 marks). Application letter 3 guidelines (3 marks). Persuasive request 3 appeals names (3 marks). Define 'agreement' in context of Indirect organizational plan (5 marks). Minutes of meetings True/False (5 marks). MCQs: Committee definition, Agenda definition, Negotiation strategies (Win-lose, Lose-win, Win-win).
Topics covered: Negotiations, Persuasive writing, Resume, Collection letter. All questions were true/false, long, and short. Mostly quiz 3 or 4 MCQs. Files were helpful.
MCQs mostly easy. Short questions: 2 True/False, Resume topic, Sales letter. Long questions: 5 uses of memo report, Blanks, True/False, Presentation topic.
MCQs from handouts and files. Questions: Define medical reports, 2 biological types of formal report, Steps to impress customer. True/False questions were present.
MCQs easy from handouts. Short & Long questions had True/False. Definitions: AGENDA, Advisory, Ad Hoc. 5 psychological barriers for negotiation. Good news Plan.

MCQs all from handouts. Short: Blanks from Business report, Good news plan meaning, Body language of presenter, True/false from collection letter & thesis writing. Long: True/false from collection letter, Blanks from Resume, 5 types of buffer, True/false from negotiation strategy. Focus on handouts and ignore excessive examples.

MCQs from handouts and conceptual. Short: Chronological resume's format, Tone of request letters, Three C's for expanding credit privileges. Long: True/False questions, Five psychological barriers in negotiating.

MCQs from handouts. Short: Difference between cover letter and traditional letters, Parts of memorandum, 3Cs of thesis. Long: Abstract in thesis, Three stages of interview, Selection stages, Buffer avoidance.
